musicalRole: Pioneered the melodic, vocal role of electric bass in Lusophone African popular music

title: Semba — Kabetula & Kasukuta Carnival Bass (Luanda/Bengo)
description: Fast, aggressive carnival rhythm from Luanda and Bengo provinces. High-intensity syncopation and galloping 16th-note figures that drive carnival street dancers and influenced fast modern Kizomba variations.
focus: Fast, continuous 16th-note syncopated stamina and percussive ghost notes
musicalRole: Carnival street band bass driver locking with deep surdo and snare drums

title: Semba — Semba Foundational Bassline (Angola)
description: The primary parent rhythm of Kizomba. Fast, playful, and percussive 2/4 (or fast 4/4) Angolan pulse featuring syncopated octave leaps, chromatic drop-ins, and strong upbeats that lock with dikanza (scraper) and congas.
focus: Playful syncopated octave bouncing and 16th-note pickups characteristic of Angolan Semba
musicalRole: Primary melodic bass foundation driving traditional Angolan Semba and live Kizomba bands
